text:
Maya (Product): Quick sync: Ruth says BlueHarbor wants a pilot for per-tenant routing + geo-fallback. They asked for a one-month SLA trial and a checklist to sign. Need scope + minimal safeguards.
Jon (Eng): Can do a pilot that uses soft-affinity + weighted fallback. Hard isolation (reserved pools) is a bigger lift.
Priya (Arch): Agree. Soft-affinity requires: routing policy DSL, tenant affinity tags, fallback mapping, and eviction/quota rules. Also need metrics per-tenant.
Evan (SRE): Ops asks: budget cap controls, cold-start warmers, prewarmed KV caches across target regions. We should document expected cold window and cost spike.
Ruth (Sales): BlueHarbor will consider pilot if we promise clear rollback and a cost cap. They also want a runbook for region failover for their legal team.
Leo (Legal): For the SLA trial, we can do an exceptions clause with measured metrics and a trial cap. Need acceptance criteria spelled out.
Maya (Product): Proposal: Pilot = region-affinity routing + per-route latency tier SLOs + automated fallback to nearest compatible variant. No hard reserved pool. Pilot terms: 4-week window, budget cap, 99.9% availability objective, telemetry export.
Jon (Eng): Dev plan: routing DSL sketch (week1), runtime affinity hook + simple placement (week2), telemetry tagging + dashboard (week3), canary rollout + rollback (week4). Minimal docs accompany.
Priya (Arch): Include compatibility matrix for model variants and a tenant eviction policy: graceful shedding, priority queues, and emergency throttle.
Evan (SRE): I'll draft runbook items: how to trigger manual failover, how to scale warmers, and monitoring checks for KV sync lag. Add an automated budget cap enforcement too.
Ruth (Sales): I'll ask BlueHarbor to rank must-haves vs nice-to-haves and confirm budget limit. Also ask legal if they need data residency terms.
Leo (Legal): If data residency is a must, pilot might need region-specific routing only. That changes scope. Please surface ASAP.
Maya (Product): Action items: Jon -> DSL POC by Fri; Priya -> arch note w/ risks + compatibility by Mon; Evan -> ops checklist + burn simulation runbook by Tue; Ruth -> customer must-have list by call.
Jon (Eng): tagging @ci-bot to create a canary pipeline for route changes.
ci-bot: Created pipeline: tenant-routing-pilot-1747778000 (stages: lint, integration, telemetry-validate, canary-traffic).
Evan (SRE): One more: telemetry needs token-level p50/p95/p99 for each tenant route and region. Without that legal/ops can't certify SLA.
Priya (Arch): Noted. Also adding guardrail: default eviction threshold at 70% region utilization and cooling window of 10m. Can tweak per-tenant in pilot.
Jon (Eng): I'll prototype the DSL with examples: "affinity: region(us-west-2); fallback: nearest; sla: latency-100ms". Will surface compatibility constraints.
Ruth (Sales): If we can commit to pilot timeline (4 weeks) and a clear rollback, BlueHarbor says they're likely to sign pilot MSA.
Maya (Product): Great. After BlueHarbor call, we'll finalize the pilot statement of work and paste a one-paragraph summary into the MSA. Keep updates here short so I can copy them over.
Ruth (Sales): ACK. I'll loop in BlueHarbor tonight.
Jon (Eng): PR will land in a draft state; will link it here.
Maya (Product): Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the customer call and lock the SOW.
Ruth (Sales): Thanks team :thumbsup:
__notes: Slack thread: product-led negotiation for tenant routing pilot. Short messages, action items, timeline, canary/ops considerations, legal constraints, and a customer sign-off flow.
